title: La cadena de valor de la inteligencia artificial: una perspectiva crítica / The artificial intelligence value chain: A critical appraisal
key_points: The article analyses the role of the 'artificial intelligence value chain' concept in EU AI regulation, especially the AI Act, and in recent EU programmes (Compass for Competitiveness, AI Continent Action Plan, Apply AI Strategy, Digital Omnibus on AI).

It compares three legal approaches to AI regulation: the EU's holistic risk-based model, the principles-based UK/Commonwealth model (with Australia and Canada as mixed cases), and the US fragmented/sectoral model under recent presidential executive orders.

It traces the value chain concept to Porter's Competitive Advantage (1985), noting it was built for corporate strategy and that AI value chain versions tend to place ethical and legal aspects only among support activities.

The author argues for redefining the AI value chain to capture intangible, non-monetizable dimensions such as language, culture, and ethical and legal values, and proposes an ethical and legal value chain to preserve democratic values and the rule of law.

The article also addresses the relationship between AI and natural languages, and sets out its structure: sections on frameworks, value chain concepts, obstacles, the EU AI Act, EU innovation strategy, the ethical-legal chain, and language.
